title: MotorcycleGraph NPE after an intersection: ChartWalker.nextEdgeHit returns null (fandisk figure_10, hand figure_6)
description:
Two meshes crash in the motorcycle event simulation with the same stack:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field "parametricDelta" because "edgeHit" is null
  at MotorcycleGraph.enqueueNextEvent(MotorcycleGraph.java:481)
  at MotorcycleGraph.handleIntersection(MotorcycleGraph.java:610)
  at MotorcycleGraph.build(MotorcycleGraph.java:394)
  at MotorcycleGraph.evaluate(MotorcycleGraph.java:293)
  at QuadLayoutEngine.buildMotorcycleGraph(QuadLayoutEngine.java:292)
```

- ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/fandisk_in_tri.off: `[motorcycle] event simulation: ports=112 queue=112`, reported as failed-to-load, then the same NPE escapes on the main thread.
- ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_6/hand_in_tri.off: `[motorcycle] event simulation: ports=152 queue=152`, uncaught on the main thread.

ChartWalker.nextEdgeHit is documented to return null when the level line leaves the face only behind the current position (corner-tangent or inconsistent state), and the launch path handles that. handleIntersection does not: after advanceStateAlongLevel moves the surviving trace to the intersection point (event.u, event.v) it calls enqueueNextEvent, which dereferences the hit unconditionally. When the intersection lies on a face edge or corner, the advanced state can sit exactly on the boundary with the direction pointing out of the face, so nextEdgeHit sees no forward crossing. The fix is to route the post-intersection state through the same edge or vertex transition the walker uses on launch (crossVertex / crossEdge) before enqueueing, or to treat a null hit as 'the trace continues in the neighbouring face' rather than crashing. Related to the raycast dead-ends fixed in PATCH-93, which addressed the launch path only.

Also, the fandisk log shows the failure is reported by the scene and then rethrown, so the scene's failed-to-load handling does not actually stop the exception. That belongs with the entry-point hardening in the Block binary-OFF ticket but should be checked here too.
definition-of-done: 1. fandisk (figure_10) and hand (figure_6) load in QuadLayoutScene through buildPatchSurfaces. 2. handleIntersection handles a null nextEdgeHit by transitioning the trace across the edge or vertex it sits on, and a log counter reports how often that path fires. 3. The count of traces and T-junctions on hand (figure_6) is recorded on the ticket before and after the fix so the change is visible. 4. The previously loading meshes (rockerarm, botijo, elk) still produce the same motorcycle statistics.
testing-plan: 1. Reproduce on hand_in_tri.off with a launch.json entry; log the trace id, face, (u,v) and direction at the failing enqueueNextEvent. 2. Confirm the state is on an edge or corner of its current face. 3. Implement the transition and rerun both meshes. 4. Screenshots of both under tmp/. 5. Run the motorcycle tests in ixdar-app/src/test.
unknowns: hand (figure_6) now clears the motorcycle stage but fails downstream at SnappingCarve.placeNodes:191 - 'T-mesh nodes 40 and 41 both landed on copy vertex 2699'. Independent of this fix: the same error with the same node ids and the same copy vertex appeared under a completely different arrangement (1744 vs 1745 patches, 1851 vs 1861 nodes) during diagnosis. Nodes 40/41 are spawn-origin nodes created before the simulation runs.

fandisk (figure_10) now clears the motorcycle stage but fails downstream at QuantizedMeshGrid.build:238 - 'quantization ILP INFEASIBLE'. Its arrangement is poor (607 of 2465 cycles are valid rectangles, 5334 hop-turn law violations) because 24 of 112 traces terminate at degenerate chart cells; the chart-degeneracy those cells come from is upstream of this ticket.

botijo (figure_?) motorcycle stage is perfect (3382/3382 valid rectangles, 0 law violations, stall counter 0) but the pipeline then fails in the zero-arc collapse with 'arc 4824 could not be re-routed onto vertex 11156 ... without fencing in the fan' - the same failure class as PATCH-111, and unreachable from this change since the stall path never fires on botijo.
changes-made: Root cause: not drift. After an intersection, advanceStateAlongLevel leaves the trace exactly (bit-identically) on the face's own forward exit crossing, so ChartWalker.nextEdgeHit's strict advance > 0 test rejects it and every other crossing is behind. Both hand cases logged advance == 0.0 exactly on an edge interior (t=0.537 and t=0.222 along the edge), never at a corner and never outside the face.

Why the intersection lands there: the other segment is COLLINEAR (same axis, bit-identical iso level), and FaceSegmentIndex.intersectSegments's axisA == axisB branch clamps the contact to the other chord's endpoint (Math.min/max with spanStart), which is exactly the face exit point an earlier visit produced. The trace had also just ping-ponged A -> B -> A through a chart cell with a degenerate image (a 1-ulp chord in B), so it re-entered A at its exit point with the direction pointing out of A.

Fix: ChartWalker.stalledExitHit(State) reports the level crossing nearest the current point at zero parametric length (all three edges considered, incoming included), and MotorcycleGraph.crossStalledBoundary transports the trace through it with crossVertex for a corner hit and crossEdge otherwise, then retries nextEdgeHit in the neighbouring face. The candidate enumeration nextEdgeHit and stalledExitHit share was factored into ChartWalker.collectLevelCrossings/crossingHit; nextEdgeHit's behaviour is line-for-line unchanged.

Log counters: [motorcycle-diag] stalledBoundaryCrossings=N stalledTerminations=M, printed only when nonzero. hand: crossings=2 terminations=2. fandisk: crossings=24 terminations=24. rockerarm, botijo, elk: 0 (the path never fires, so their motorcycle statistics are untouched).

One crossing per trace (Trace.stalledCrossingTaken), then terminate. Measured: with a budget of 8 the same 24 fandisk traces still terminated after 192 crossings (4699 cycles / 605 valid rectangles / 10374 law violations) versus 2465 cycles / 607 valid / 5334 violations at one crossing. Every stall is a two-face bounce with no correct continuation, so a larger budget only pollutes the arrangement.

hand (figure_6) before: traces=152 spawned, queue=152, then NPE at MotorcycleGraph.java:481 - no arcs, nodes or patches produced at all. After: 12750 events, 0 traces alive at queue end, arcs=3640 nodes=1861 patches=1745, 1745 cycles / 1705 valid rectangles / 0 unresolved, flat (T-junction) hops=234, Def 3.1 rectangularity violations=0, 0.15s.
fandisk (figure_10) before: traces=112, queue=112, same NPE. After: 14109 events, 0 alive at end, arcs=7741 nodes=3938 patches=2465, 2465 cycles / 607 valid rectangles / 0 unresolved.

Unchanged meshes, motorcycle stage: rockerarm 120 traces, 2706 arcs, 1383 nodes, 1323 cycles all valid, 0 law violations. botijo 328 traces, 6928 arcs, 3538 nodes, 3382 cycles all valid, 0 violations. elk 320 traces, 6192 arcs, 3176 nodes, 3016 cycles all valid, 0 violations. Stall counter zero on all three.

Test: ixdar-app/test/unit/mesh/ChartWalkerStalledExitTest.java - two hand-authored triangles sharing an edge, no mesh file. Pins nextEdgeHit returning null on the stalled state, stalledExitHit naming the edge under it at zero length, crossEdge continuing into the neighbour face, and nextEdgeHit's unchanged forward/backward behaviour from inside the face. Full unit suite: Tests run: 227, Failures: 0, Errors: 0.

Launch entries: 'PATCH-109: mcg-exam hand' and 'PATCH-109: mcg-exam fandisk' (scene mcg-exam, which runs exactly to buildMotorcycleGraph). Both render; screenshots at tmp/launch-hand.png, tmp/launch-fandisk.png, tmp/mcg-hand.png, tmp/mcg-fandisk.png.

Answers unknown 1: the intersection's (u,v) is EXACTLY on the face's exit edge - the edge-crossing advance computed to 0.0 bit-exactly in both hand cases. Drift does not push the state outside the face; the intersection is snapped onto the exit point by the collinear-overlap clamp.
